data.label: Receive CSV File
data.rationale: This is a deterministic trigger event based on file receipt. It requires no AI, no uncertainty handling, and can be implemented with a simple event listener or file watcher, so L0 is appropriate.
conditions: fires when a new CSV file is detected
file extension must be .csv or MIME must indicate text/csv
data.description: Start the validation workflow when a CSV file is received for processing.
data.errorHandling: If the file cannot be accessed or is not a CSV, emit a terminal validation error and stop the workflow. Retry only for transient file-lock or read errors.

data.label: Parse CSV Content
data.rationale: CSV parsing is deterministic syntax handling with no need for ML or language understanding. Standard parsing libraries can reliably convert the file into rows and columns, so L0 is sufficient.
conditions: requires readable file path or file stream
output must include header row, parsed rows, and parse metadata
data.description: Read the incoming CSV file and load its rows and columns into a structured format.
data.errorHandling: On malformed CSV, capture parser line/column details and return a structured parse error. Retry once for transient I/O issues; do not retry syntax errors.

data.label: Check Expected Columns
data.rationale: This is a rule-based schema comparison: compare the observed column names against the expected list and flag missing or extra columns as needed. No learning or language reasoning is required, so L0 fits.
conditions: schema must define expected columns
input must include parsed header names
data.description: Verify that the CSV contains all required columns defined by the schema.
data.errorHandling: If required columns are missing, record them as validation errors and continue downstream checks only when the remaining schema permits row-level validation. If headers are unreadable, stop with schema validation failure.

data.label: Validate Data Types
data.rationale: Type validation is deterministic: each value can be checked against expected formats such as integer, date, boolean, or string. This is classic rule-based validation and does not require ML or an LLM, so L0 is appropriate.
conditions: schema must define per-column types
skip type checks for columns missing from headers
data.description: Check whether each column's values match the expected schema data types.
data.errorHandling: Collect per-cell type mismatches without failing the whole workflow. If parsing of a field fails unexpectedly, log row/column context and continue validating remaining rows.

data.label: Flag Missing Required Values
data.rationale: Checking for null or empty values in required fields is fully deterministic and rule-based. It is a straightforward validation step with no uncertainty, so L0 is sufficient.
conditions: schema must define required fields
only evaluate fields present in the parsed data
data.description: Identify null or empty values in required fields and record them as validation errors.
data.errorHandling: Treat missing required values as non-fatal validation errors and append them to the error list. If the row is structurally invalid, mark the row as unprocessable and continue with other rows.

data.label: Check Numeric Ranges
data.rationale: Range checking is a deterministic comparison against predefined bounds. It requires no machine learning or language reasoning, so L0 is the correct classification.
conditions: schema must define min/max bounds for numeric fields
only run on values that passed numeric type validation
data.description: Verify that numeric values fall within the acceptable bounds defined by the schema.
data.errorHandling: If a value is non-numeric, rely on the type-validation error and skip range evaluation for that cell. Record out-of-range values with expected bounds and actual value.

data.label: Collect Validation Errors
data.rationale: Aggregating validation errors is deterministic data collection and merging. It does not involve ambiguity, prediction, or language generation, so L0 is appropriate.
conditions: input error arrays must be normalized to a common schema
deduplicate repeated errors by row/column/code
data.description: Combine all issues found across column, type, required field, and range checks into a single error set.
data.errorHandling: If aggregation fails due to malformed error objects, fall back to a raw passthrough list and include an aggregation warning in the report.

data.label: Generate Validation Report
data.rationale: Although this step produces formatted output, the report content is directly derived from collected validation results and can be rendered deterministically using templates or structured serialization. No generative AI is required, so L0 is sufficient.
conditions: requires aggregated error list and summary statistics
must include file name, total rows, error counts, and detailed findings
data.description: Create a report listing all validation errors found in the CSV file.
data.errorHandling: If formatted rendering fails, fall back to plain JSON report output with the same validation details. Ensure the report is still produced even when formatting templates are unavailable.

data.label: Finish Validation
data.rationale: This is a terminal workflow step that returns the completed report. It is purely procedural and deterministic, so L0 applies.
conditions: report must be generated successfully or via fallback JSON output
data.description: Complete the workflow and return the validation report result.
data.errorHandling: If persistence or return payload delivery fails, log the failure and preserve the generated report artifact for retry or manual retrieval.

data.condition: CSV syntax error or unrecoverable I/O failure

message: Low-risk, deterministic CSV validation workflow. Kept standard logging with step-level snapshots for observability, tight latency/error thresholds due to customer-facing data quality impact, and moderate alerting via Slack and email. No human gate was added because the workflow is fully rule-based and non-destructive; validation failures are already captured and reported deterministically.

workflow.workflowBrief: Validate incoming CSV files: check that the file has the expected columns, verify data types match the schema, flag any null values in required fields, check that numeric values are within acceptable ranges, and generate a validation report listing all errors found.
